unit.title: HTML: your first tags
unit.description: What HTML does, tags that open and close, paragraphs, headings, nesting, the .html file

cards.definition:

cards.example:
marks a main heading,

a paragraph.

cards.definition:
Most content sits between a start marker and an end marker with a slash:

then

.
cards.example:
Hello

: the text Hello is wrapped by the pair.

cards.definition: The whole unit made of the opening tag, the content and the closing tag.
Holds a block of ordinary text; the browser starts each one on a new line, with space around it.
Six levels of titles, from the most important (h1, biggest by default) to the least (h6).
cards.example: One <h1> for the page title, <h2> for each section.

cards.definition: Putting an element inside another one; the inner element must be closed before the outer one.
A plain text file whose name ends in .html; a browser opens it and displays it as a page.
cards.example: index.html is usually the home page of a site.

choices: Describing the content and structure of a page
Choosing the colors and the spacing
Making the page react to clicks
Storing the data on a server
exercises.explain: HTML says what each piece of content is: a heading, a paragraph, a link, an image. CSS styles it, JavaScript makes it react.
whyWrong: Colors and spacing are the job of CSS.
Reacting to clicks is the job of JavaScript.
Data is stored on the server, in a database, not in HTML.

exercises.prompt: What does the browser show for this line?
choices: The text Hello, as a paragraph
exercises.explain: Tags are instructions for the browser, not text to display. Only what sits between them appears on the page.
whyWrong: The tags are read by the browser, not displayed.
p is the name of the tag; it is not displayed.
This line is valid HTML.

exercises.explain:
A closing tag repeats the name of the opening tag with a slash after the angle bracket:

then

.
whyWrong: opens a paragraph; it does not close it.

The slash goes right after the first angle bracket:

.
HTML has no <end> tag.

exercises.prompt: <h1> shows a bigger title than <h3> by default.
exercises.explain: Headings go from h1 (most important, biggest) to h6 (least important, smallest).

exercises.prompt: Which tag should hold the main title of the page?
exercises.explain: The main visible title of the page goes in <h1>. Sections then use <h2>, sub-sections <h3>.
whyWrong: h6 is the smallest, least important heading.
is for ordinary text, not a title.
<title> is the name shown in the browser tab, not on the page.

exercises.prompt: How many paragraphs does the browser display?
exercises.explain:
Each

element is one paragraph. A heading is not a paragraph.
whyWrong:
There are two

elements, so two paragraphs.
The <h1> is a heading, not a paragraph.

Count the

opening tags: there are two.

exercises.explain: The inner element must close first: open p, open strong, close strong, close p. Like boxes inside boxes.
whyWrong: strong was opened last, so it must be closed first.
The second <strong> has no slash: it opens again instead of closing.
p was opened inside strong, so it must close before strong.

exercises.prompt: Build a paragraph that contains the text Welcome.
exercises.explain:
Welcome

: the opening tag, the content, the closing tag with its slash.

exercises.prompt: The second paragraph is displayed in bold too. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explain: The second has no slash, so it opens bold text again instead of closing it. Write .

exercises.prompt: What must the name of a page file end with to open as a web page?
exercises.explain: A page file ends in .html (for example index.html). A browser opens it and displays it as a page.
whyWrong: A .txt file is shown as raw text, tags included.
.css files hold styles, not pages.
.page is not a web file type.

exercises.prompt:
In

Hi

, the whole thing, tags and text, is called an element.
exercises.explain: An element is the opening tag, the content and the closing tag together.
